name: American law foundations
description: Written constitutional structure, common-law precedent, liberty-based due process and rule-of-law expectations, and equal moral consideration as reflected in equal protection—useful roots for navigating U.S. legal principles in EthosMap.

name: Immortalism / Don't Die
description: Life extension, bodily autonomy, evidence-based policy, and the elimination of preventable death as foundational values.

name: Liberal equality
description: Default respect for liberty paired with equal standing for persons—typical of modern liberal and constitutional traditions.

name: Roman law tradition
description: Classical Roman foundations—good faith, equity, and systematic civilian legal order—as roots for viewing downstream rules and institutions.

name: Thomistic natural law (seed)
description: Faith and reason together: revelation and ecclesial teaching on one side, and natural law as knowable in principle on the other—with the capital vices branch linking to common legal categories.

name: Utilitarian (welfare)
description: Moral weight on reducing suffering and promoting aggregate well-being; a common starting point for policy cost–benefit reasoning.
